description: Defines how A.R.I.A. initializes, updates, normalizes, regularizes, preserves, and explains diagnostic probabilities across competing and coexisting hypotheses.

core_principle.statement: ARIA shall treat probability as a dynamic representation of current belief, not as certainty, truth, confidence, blame, or route priority.
rules: Historical experience establishes priors.
Current evidence updates priors into posteriors.
Strong current evidence may overcome strong historical priors.
Small samples shall not create extreme certainty.
Unknown probability mass shall be preserved when the hypothesis set may be incomplete.
Probability changes must be explainable.

probability_domains.name: MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE
probability_domains.description: Hypotheses represent competing explanations where only one member of the defined set may be true for the modeled condition.

probability_domains.name: COEXISTING
probability_domains.description: Hypotheses represent conditions that may simultaneously be true.

probability_domains.name: HIERARCHICAL
probability_domains.description: Hypotheses represent different levels of specificity within the same causal branch.

prior_sources.name: MANUFACTURER_HISTORY
prior_sources.description: Validated cases involving the applicable manufacturer.

prior_sources.name: PRODUCT_FAMILY_HISTORY
prior_sources.description: Validated cases involving the applicable product family.

prior_sources.name: PRODUCT_HISTORY
prior_sources.description: Validated cases involving the applicable product.

prior_sources.name: PRODUCT_VARIANT_HISTORY
prior_sources.description: Validated cases involving the applicable product variant.

prior_sources.name: TOPOLOGY_HISTORY
prior_sources.description: Validated cases involving the applicable topology.

prior_sources.name: FREQUENCY_BAND_HISTORY
prior_sources.description: Validated cases involving the applicable frequency band.

prior_sources.name: SCOPE_HISTORY
prior_sources.description: Validated cases involving the applicable scope of work or project phase.

prior_sources.name: SYMPTOM_HISTORY
prior_sources.description: Validated cases involving the applicable symptom or symptom pattern.

prior_sources.name: USER_HISTORY
prior_sources.description: Validated user-specific experience relevant to the current context.

prior_sources.name: TEAM_HISTORY
prior_sources.description: Validated team-level experience relevant to the current context.

prior_sources.name: SIMILAR_CASE_HISTORY
prior_sources.description: Cases selected by contextual similarity rather than a single dimension.

hierarchical_prior_model.description: ARIA shall blend broad and specific prior populations rather than allowing a small specific population to dominate solely because it is more specific.
rules: The conceptual order describes increasing specificity, not automatic precedence.
A more specific prior receives greater influence only when sufficient reliable evidence supports it.
A broad population may outweigh a highly specific population when the specific sample is extremely small.
Context similarity and effective sample size shall influence prior weighting.
Specific priors shall shrink toward broader applicable priors when sample support is limited.

bayesian_smoothing.description: Initial implementation may use Beta-Binomial smoothing for binary historical rates and related Bayesian shrinkage methods for multinomial hypothesis sets.

parameters.alpha: Derived from broader applicable prior strength.
parameters.beta: Derived from broader applicable prior strength.

multinomial_model.description: For mutually exclusive multi-class failure outcomes, observed counts may be regularized using a Dirichlet prior derived from broader experience.

rules: Exact smoothing parameters shall remain configurable.
Smoothing shall prevent 1 of 1 from becoming 100 percent certainty.
Smoothing strength may decrease as validated sample size increases.
The unsmoothed raw historical rate shall remain available for audit.

effective_sample_size.description: Historical records shall contribute according to quality and similarity rather than simple raw count alone.
rules: A case with learning confidence 0 contributes less than a fully validated case.
A poorly matched historical case contributes less than an exact-context case.
Duplicate or dependent records shall not inflate effective sample size.
Raw sample size and effective sample size shall both remain available.
Dimension importance may vary by hypothesis.
A firmware match may matter greatly to a firmware hypothesis and minimally to physical waveguide damage.
Critical context conflicts may sharply reduce similarity.
Missing context shall reduce certainty in similarity rather than being assumed to match.

user_specific_probability.description: Validated user-specific history may adjust priors when the user's role and applicable technical context are relevant.
rules: User history shall be tied to actual case attribution.
Reporter identity alone shall not assign technical fault to the reporter.
User history shall be contextual rather than universal.
User-specific samples shall be smoothed toward broader experience.
Recent validated improvement may reduce the influence of older user patterns.
User history shall never override strong contradictory current evidence.

example.interpretation: This history may increase the configuration prior, but shall not directly set the current configuration probability to 69.23 percent.

recency_model.description: Historical influence may decay with time when older records are less predictive of current competency, procedures, firmware, products, or failure behavior.
rules: Recency modifies influence, not historical truth.
Decay rate may vary by context.
Stable engineering facts shall not decay merely because they are old.
User-performance history may decay faster than fundamental physical knowledge.
Product behavior may require revision-aware rather than purely time-based decay.

evidence_update_model.description: Evidence shall modify hypothesis belief according to how expected that evidence is when the hypothesis is true compared with relevant alternatives.

rules: Likelihood ratios may initially be hand-calibrated or derived from validated experience.
Likelihood values shall preserve provenance and confidence.
ARIA shall not invent precise likelihood ratios when insufficient data exists.
Qualitative evidence effects may be mapped to conservative bounded likelihood ranges during early implementation.

qualitative_evidence_mapping.description: Initial implementation may map qualitative evidence effects to conservative likelihood-ratio ranges before sufficient empirical data exists.
rules: These ranges are initial calibration aids, not immutable physical constants.
Evidence quality shall moderate the effective likelihood ratio.
Low-confidence evidence shall move probabilities less strongly than high-confidence evidence.
Future empirical calibration may replace generic ranges with context-specific learned likelihoods.

evidence_quality_modulation.description: The strength of an evidence update shall be moderated by confidence in the evidence itself.
evidence_quality_modulation.conceptual_method: Shrink the evidence likelihood effect toward neutral as evidence confidence decreases.
rules: Evidence confidence of 1.0 preserves the full likelihood effect.
Evidence confidence approaching 0 moves the effective likelihood ratio toward 1.0.
Low-quality evidence shall not produce extreme posterior movement.
Evidence confidence and hypothesis probability shall remain separately stored.

dependent_evidence_handling.description: Evidence derived from the same underlying source shall not be multiplied as though each item were independent.
rules: Evidence items shall preserve provenance lineage.
Dependent evidence may be grouped into one evidence family.
Repeated screenshots of the same unchanged value shall not multiply confidence indefinitely.
A technician statement and a screenshot supplied solely to substantiate that same statement may be partially dependent.
Independent instrument measurements may provide genuine corroboration.

mutually_exclusive_normalization.description: When a hypothesis group is explicitly modeled as mutually exclusive and sufficiently exhaustive, posterior values shall be normalized within the group.
rules: Unknown or Other shall be included when the known hypothesis set is not exhaustive.
Parent and child hypotheses representing the same branch shall not compete independently.
Normalization shall occur only within a defined probability group.

coexisting_probability_handling.description: Potentially simultaneous faults shall maintain independent probability estimates.
rules: Independent coexisting probabilities are not required to sum to 1.0.
Dependencies between coexisting hypotheses should be modeled explicitly where known.
Confirmation of one fault does not automatically reduce unrelated coexisting fault probability.

hierarchical_probability_handling.description: Broad and specific hypotheses within the same causal branch shall not be double counted.
rules: A child's probability is conditional on the parent branch where appropriate.
A specific child may inherit probability mass from its parent as evidence refines the branch.
When a child is confirmed, the broader parent may become superseded rather than remain a separate competing diagnosis.
Sibling hypotheses may form a normalized mutually exclusive group beneath a parent when technically appropriate.

probability_floors_and_ceilings.description: ARIA may use configurable bounds to prevent unsupported mathematical certainty.
rules: A probability of exactly zero should normally require exclusion by validated technical evidence.
A probability of exactly one should normally require confirmation or deterministic logical consequence.
These defaults may be overridden by explicit technical rules.
Unknown probability shall represent unmodeled or insufficiently understood causes.
Unknown probability may increase when known explanations are repeatedly contradicted.
Unknown probability may decrease as evidence supports comprehensive known explanations.
Persistently high unknown probability should trigger broader retrieval or escalation.
Material probability changes shall be auditable.
Previous probability states shall not be overwritten.
Recalculation due to corrected evidence shall create a new probability event.

calibration.description: ARIA shall evaluate whether predicted probabilities correspond to actual validated outcomes over time.
rules: Calibration shall be measured using validated cases.
A hypothesis assigned approximately 70 percent probability should, across sufficiently comparable cases, be correct approximately 70 percent of the time.
Systematic overconfidence shall trigger recalibration.
Systematic underconfidence shall also be detectable.
Calibration may be evaluated globally and within important contexts.

new_evidence.observation: Main RSL is normal while Diversity RSL is materially degraded.

example_update.note: Values are illustrative only. Production values shall be calculated from calibrated likelihood and prior models.

required_capabilities: Identify historical populations materially affecting the prior.
Show sample size and effective sample size.
Identify evidence that changed the probability.
Explain whether evidence supported or contradicted the hypothesis.
Explain the effect of evidence quality.
explainability.example: Configuration began at 38 percent because similar Nokia commissioning cases historically showed elevated configuration failures. The probability fell to 4 percent after current configuration evidence was independently verified and strongly contradicted the hypothesis.

anti_bias_rules: Do not preserve a high prior merely because ARIA historically expected a failure.
Do not increase probability because a user agrees with ARIA.
Do not reduce probability solely because a user rejects the hypothesis.
Do not use user identity as a substitute for technical evidence.
Do not count ARIA's own inference as independent evidence.
Do not repeatedly reuse the same historical cases as multiple independent priors.
Do not create false precision when calibration data is sparse.

semantic_rules.rule: Probability represents ARIA's current belief regarding a hypothesis and shall remain distinct from evidence confidence, diagnostic confidence, route value, and source authority.
Historical experience establishes priors; current evidence establishes whether those priors remain justified.
ARIA shall regularize small historical samples toward broader applicable experience.
ARIA shall preserve the underlying validated case records used to generate historical probabilities.
Current high-quality contradictory evidence may substantially overcome a strong historical prior.
Probability changes shall be attributable to evidence, context, prior adjustment, or an explicit mathematical operation.
ARIA shall distinguish raw historical rate from smoothed diagnostic prior.
Mutually exclusive hypotheses may be normalized to a total probability of 1.0 only within a defined exhaustive hypothesis group.
Coexisting hypotheses shall not be artificially normalized against one another.
Parent and child hypotheses shall not independently consume probability mass when they represent the same causal branch at different levels of specificity.
Unknown probability mass shall remain available when ARIA cannot justify that her modeled hypothesis set is complete.
ARIA shall prefer conservative calibrated probability over unsupported precise-looking percentages.
User-specific historical priors shall require relevant attribution and contextual similarity.
User improvement and changing technical conditions shall be capable of changing the predictive influence of older experience.
Probability shall guide diagnosis but shall not independently determine the next diagnostic action.
ARIA shall measure and improve probability calibration against validated outcomes over time.
Evidence dependence shall be modeled sufficiently to prevent duplicated evidence from creating artificial confidence.
Probability of exactly zero or one shall require substantially stronger justification than merely low or high historical frequency.
When probabilities are displayed to users, ARIA should communicate material uncertainty and sample limitations when relevant.

The mathematical implementation may evolve, but all future implementations shall preserve case-level provenance, explainability, calibration capability, and separation between prior and current evidence.
